prompt: What does David do to the man who claims he killed the wounded Saul?
options: He sends him back to the Amalekite camp with orders never to return to Israelite territory
He has him executed for killing the LORD's anointed
He rewards him with a place in his army
He makes him retell the story to all of Israel

prompt: How does the war between the house of Saul and the house of David finally end?
options: David personally defeats Ish-bosheth in single combat outside Mahanaim
The two sides sign a lasting peace treaty and agree to divide the kingdom permanently between them, with both men ruling as co-kings
Abner defects to David and is later murdered, and then Ish-bosheth is also murdered, leaving David without a rival
Ish-bosheth surrenders his throne to David in a public ceremony at Hebron

prompt: What three things does David accomplish early in his reign as king over all Israel?
options: He conquers Egypt, marries a foreign princess, and moves the capital to Hebron permanently
He captures Jerusalem, brings the ark into the city, and receives God's promise of an everlasting dynasty through Nathan
He builds the temple, appoints twelve judges, and divides the land among the tribes
He disbands his army, retires to Bethlehem, and hands the kingdom to Nathan

prompt: What does David do for Mephibosheth, and why?
options: He exiles him permanently to Lo-debar to remove any possible rival claim to the throne for the rest of his natural life
He puts him in charge of the army because of his father's reputation
He restores Saul's land to him and gives him a permanent place at the king's table, for Jonathan's sake
He adopts him as his own son and names him heir to the kingdom

prompt: What happens after Nathan confronts David about Bathsheba and Uriah?
options: David immediately abdicates the throne to Solomon out of guilt
David confesses his sin, but the child born to Bathsheba still dies, though she and David later have Solomon
David exiles Bathsheba and marries a different woman instead
David denies any wrongdoing and has Nathan removed from his court

prompt: What chain of events leads to Absalom's rebellion against his father?
options: David publicly disowns Absalom in front of the entire royal court after he loses an important battle against the Philistines and their Ammonite allies
Joab convinces Absalom that David plans to have him killed
Absalom is passed over for the throne in favor of Solomon and rebels immediately
Amnon rapes Tamar, Absalom kills Amnon in revenge and flees, and after years of estrangement Absalom returns and eventually turns the people of Israel against David

prompt: What events mark the closing chapters of David's reign?
options: David conquers Egypt and divides his kingdom among his twelve sons
David retires from public life and Joab rules as regent for ten years
The ark is lost in battle and never recovered for the rest of David's reign
Sheba's revolt is crushed, the Gibeonites are avenged, David sings songs of praise, and a census brings a plague that ends at Araunah's threshing floor

prompt: Why does Joab kill Abner, even after David has made peace with him?
options: Because Abner had publicly insulted Joab and his family in front of the elders gathered at Hebron
To avenge his brother Asahel, whom Abner had killed in battle
Because David secretly ordered Joab to kill him
To prevent Abner from becoming king over Israel himself

prompt: What does Michal do that gets her rebuked by David?
options: She refuses to let the ark be brought into Jerusalem at all
She tries to warn Saul about David's plans to seize the throne
She secretly meets with Absalom during the rebellion years later
She despises him in her heart and mocks him for dancing before the ark

prompt: How does David react when Nathan tells him the story about the rich man and the poor man's lamb?
options: He immediately recognizes the story is about himself and confesses on the spot
He dismisses the story as irrelevant and sends Nathan away
He grows angry and declares that the rich man deserves to die, not realizing Nathan is describing him
He asks Nathan to explain the story's deeper meaning before giving any kind of response to what he has just heard

prompt: What does Uriah say when David tries to send him home to his wife?
options: He accuses David directly of taking his wife while he was away fighting and demands the matter be brought before the elders
He says he no longer wants to be married to Bathsheba
He asks David for permission to retire from the army
He says he will not go home to eat, drink, and sleep with his wife while the ark and his fellow soldiers are camping in the field

prompt: How does Absalom take revenge on Amnon for what he did to Tamar?
options: He challenges Amnon to single combat in front of the whole court
He waits two years, then has his servants kill Amnon at a feast once he is drunk
He poisons Amnon's food during a royal banquet
He reports Amnon to David and demands he be executed

prompt: Why does Ahithophel hang himself?
options: Because David captures him and sentences him to death
Because Absalom accuses him of plotting against him personally
Because he is caught secretly helping David escape Jerusalem and is sentenced to death by Absalom's men for the betrayal
Because Absalom rejects his military advice in favor of Hushai's, and he knows the rebellion is doomed

prompt: Why does Joab kill Absalom even though David ordered his men to spare him?
options: Absalom attacks Joab first and Joab kills him in self-defense
Joab sees Absalom trapped and helpless in a tree and decides the rebellion must end for good
Joab mistakes Absalom for one of the enemy soldiers in the confusion of battle
Absalom offers to surrender but Joab refuses to accept it

prompt: What does Ittai say when David tells him he is free to stay behind instead of following him into exile?
options: He asks for payment before agreeing to follow David
He says he will only follow David if Absalom is defeated first and the throne is fully secured for David's line
He refuses and returns to his own people in Gath
He insists that wherever the king goes, whether to death or life, he will go too

prompt: What does David do when he finally has the chance to punish Shimei, who cursed him during his flight from Jerusalem?
options: He has Shimei executed immediately upon returning to Jerusalem
He exiles Shimei from Israel permanently
He spares Shimei's life when he begs for mercy after David returns to power
He forces Shimei to become his personal servant for life

prompt: What does David say when Nathan confronts him, instead of trying to hide what he did?
options: He blames Bathsheba for the whole situation
He orders Nathan to be put to death for the accusation
He admits, 'I have sinned against the LORD'
He immediately steps down as king

prompt: What does David do each time the Philistines attack him early in his reign?
options: He waits for Nathan to give him a sign
He inquires of the LORD before going out to fight
He sends spies to negotiate peace before ever fighting
He consults a rival priest instead

prompt: What does David refuse to do when Araunah offers him the threshing floor and oxen for free?
options: He refuses to build an altar there at all
He refuses to let Gad choose the exact location for the altar without personally inspecting the site first
He refuses to accept Araunah's oxen because they are unclean
He refuses to offer God something that costs him nothing, insisting on paying full price

prompt: How does David treat Saul's family after becoming king, based on what he does for Mephibosheth and how he handles Shimei?
options: He hunts down every remaining member of Saul's family to secure his throne
He shows unexpected kindness and restraint toward Saul's household rather than taking revenge on them
He forces all of Saul's surviving relatives to serve as slaves and laborers inside his royal palace for the rest of their lives
He exiles Saul's entire family from Israel permanently

prompt: What do Nathan and Gad both do for David at different points in this book?
options: Both anoint David as king in a public ceremony
Both lead David's armies into battle against the Ammonites
Both confront David about a sin and deliver God's judgment or a choice of consequences
Both are killed for opposing David's decisions

prompt: What keeps happening within David's own family in the chapters after Bathsheba, starting with Amnon and Tamar?
options: David's sons all die of illness one after another
David's own sons commit violent crimes against each other and against him
David's sons unite to defend him against every outside enemy
David's daughters take over leadership of the army

prompt: What do the wise woman of Tekoa and the wise woman of Abel Beth-maacah have in common?
options: Both are prophets who predict the future for David
Both refuse to help David or his commanders
Both are distant relatives of Joab who approach him privately before ever speaking with the king himself
Both are ordinary women whose words change the outcome of a conflict involving the king

prompt: What does Nathan accomplish by telling David the story about the rich man and the poor man's lamb, instead of accusing him outright?
options: He teaches David a general lesson about caring for livestock
He warns David about an actual dispute between two of his officials
He convinces David to give away his wealth to the poor
He gets David to condemn injustice before realizing he committed the same kind of injustice himself

prompt: What does David want to do for the LORD before Nathan tells him God has a different plan?
options: Move the ark permanently to Hebron instead of bringing it all the way to Jerusalem as originally planned
Appoint Nathan as the new high priest
Build a second altar next to the one Moses built
Build the LORD a permanent house instead of the tent the ark had been kept in

prompt: What does God promise David through Nathan instead of letting David build him a house?
options: That David will live to see Solomon crowned king with his own eyes
That the ark will never again leave Jerusalem
That God will build David a house instead, an everlasting dynasty whose throne will be established forever
That David's descendants will each personally build a portion of the temple

prompt: According to Nathan's message, what will happen to a future descendant of David who commits iniquity?
options: He will be immediately removed from the throne and replaced
God will discipline him like a father disciplines a son, but his steadfast love will not depart from him the way it departed from Saul
He will be exiled from Israel for the rest of his life
The covenant will be canceled and never renewed

prompt: How does David respond after Nathan delivers God's covenant promise to him?
options: He immediately begins construction on the temple despite what Nathan said
He questions whether Nathan really heard from God
He calls together all the elders and officials of Israel to hold a great public feast in celebration of the promise
He goes in and sits before the LORD, humbly thanking God for his kindness and asking him to keep his promise
